Web design is a subject that seems awfully difficult than it has to be due to a lack of organization. I mean, you can pick up a bootstrap or foundation template and build a prototype in maybe a few minutes, but to build something REAL that works in the field (like voat or reddit) you need a lot more- images, fonts, icons, logos, css/javascript frameworks, etc.

I am good at backend-development, so I can't re-invent things like logos, graphics, etc, so they have to be outsourced from somewhere. So, I would like to know from you expert web designers where do you get these stuff?

Here is the list of things I've personally used before, feel free to add your own:

  • CSS Frameworks: Bootstrap, Foundation, Purecss.
  • Javascript DOM and basics: jQuery, Mustache.js, require.js.
  • Javascript MVC: Angularjs, Backbone.
  • Javascript UI: jQuery-ui, jsplumb, yui.
  • Fonts: Google Fonts SDK.
  • Icons: Fontawesome, iconfinder.
  • Free Graphics and Logos: Flickr.
  • Wordpress themes: themeforest.
Designers, where do you get your raw materials from?
Most logos and graphics will have to be created for originality and to be a symbol of the company/thing the website represents. Small things like icons and fonts can be found all over the internet.
What about using Google image search and then using Gimp to modify images to fit necessary dimension and to conform with fair use copy right requirement.

Here are some things I use...

  • Free Stock Photos: Stock Photos That Don't Suck
  • Icons iconmonstr, Endless Icons, Open Iconic
  • JQuery Plugins: Upheap
  • Fonts: Typekit (Though, it's not free.), Type Genius (Great site for finding font pairings)

Those are all I can think of at the top of my head.
